lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first; Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor Payments internship.
items.because: The order obscures the timeline for a reader scanning the section.

items.says: Coastal Marine Services takes substantial space for a role whose relevance to the product direction is not clear.
items.because: Its diesel-mechanic and inspection bullets may draw attention away from more relevant product experience.
Readers looking for relevant work history must scan past the degrees first.

items.says: The scorecards and review meeting are presented as responsibilities without a result or a clear account of what you did with them.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the work changed or judge its value.

items.says: “That discussed them” repeats the stated purpose of the monthly review meeting.
items.because: The phrase adds no useful detail.

items.says: The 30% reduction in pick errors has no stated baseline or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell the starting point or period used to measure it.

items.says: “On the new layout” repeats the layout change conveyed by redesigning slotting rules.
items.because: The extra words lengthen the bullet without clarifying the action.

items.says: The 1,800-hour result is buried after a long list of activities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the result, and the trailing “which” leaves its cause unclear.

items.says: “Taking over vendor negotiations” reads as an additional duty rather than a specific action or outcome.
items.because: It does not show what the negotiation involved or achieved.

items.says: The line attributes the reduction in time to first payment to the redesign without a comparison that establishes the effect.
items.because: Other changes during the pilot could explain the difference.

items.says: The RICE prioritization names no resulting roadmap priority or decision.
items.because: The line shows a method without making its product impact legible.

items.says: The roadmap result is buried after four process steps and does not name the priority selected.
items.because: A reader must get through the process before reaching a result that still does not reveal what the team chose.

items.says: The checkout A/B test and its conversion lift are reported twice.
items.because: Line 17 already gives the test comparison, lift and rollout, so this bullet adds no distinct result.

items.says: The claim that the food would otherwise have been thrown away is not established.
items.because: The app’s reach and redistribution total do not show what would have happened to the food without it.

items.says: The bullet does not identify what enabled pickups and redistribution.
items.because: Your specific product or operational contribution remains unclear.

items.says: The stated 150% increase is wrong; growth from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.
items.because: The increase of 750 users is 187.5% of the starting 400.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: Relative to the starting rate, it is about a 26.7% increase.

items.says: The savings estimate does not name the analysis used to produce the model.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how you arrived at the estimate.

items.says: The practicum repeats the scheduling recommendation’s pilot outcome.
items.because: Line 28 already says the client funded a pilot based on the quantified savings model.
